context.objective: Understand current work and exceptions; synthetic test only

turns.text: Walk me through a recent invoice from arrival to the point where your team's work is done.

We call it invoice approval, also invoice sign-off. An invoice arrives in our shared AP mailbox each weekday. The AP clerk enters its reference and amount in the invoice log spreadsheet, with status Received. The purpose is to obtain a documented decision on the supplier invoice. The clerk matches it to the purchase order and changes it to Checked. The department manager reviews the checked invoice and replies Approved by email. The clerk saves that email to the invoice folder and changes the log to Approved. We are finished when the approval email is filed and the status is Approved. The payment team picks up afterward; payment is a separate process and I do not know their steps. Nobody formally owns the invoice-approval outcome. A mismatched invoice goes back to the buyer for correction; I don't know how the buyer resolves it. No immovable deadline has been specified. Errors could mean paying the wrong amount. Rekeying into the log is slow and errors occur. We have an invoice checklist and a sample approval email in the AP shared folder.
Does that route change for any particular client or fund?

For fictional Fund Blue the same arrival, accountable role and finished result apply. We require two department managers to approve, because of their internal preference. The extra email chase takes about 20 minutes. I don't know whether we charge for it or who would object if it stopped. Everyone can have a mismatch sometimes, so that's a normal exception, not Fund Blue-specific.
When an invoice is found to mismatch, what actually happens next until it is either corrected or closed out?
